recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless a future BR&R decision changes the MedicinalProductDefinition operation effective date semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-17216 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request, raised against STU3 MedicinalProduct and applied for R5, asking that the MedicinalProduct effectiveDate dateTime be represented as a range because licenses and similar applicability periods can require renewal.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-17216 was found. Current-branch history shows the active MedicinalProductDefinition source introduced by 33b409a4b6 already had operation.effectiveDate typed as Period, while older pre-R5 draft MedicinalProduct source had manufacturingBusinessOperation.effectiveDate as dateTime and was later removed/renamed.
additional_context: The current build uses MedicinalProductDefinition rather than the old MedicinalProduct name: source/fhir.ini lists medicinalproductdefinition as an active resource and redirects MedicinalProduct to MedicinalProductDefinition. The R5 published StructureDefinition also has MedicinalProductDefinition.operation.effectiveDate typed as Period. Jira search found no other same-artifact issue beyond FHIR-17216, and community searches found no substantive Zulip or Confluence discussion changing the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The authoritative current source already satisfies the issue by using Period for MedicinalProductDefinition.operation.effectiveDate and describing it as a date range of applicability.
